summary: Egyptian opposition groups, including the Muslim Brotherhood, call for a national day of protests on Jan. 25, set before the Tunisian revolution, amid skepticism that Egypt is ready for its own revolution.
Egyptian Prime Minister Ahmed Shafik resigns amid continuing protests in Tahrir Square demanding the fall of the entire regime.
Libyan government forces retake control of Zawiya from rebels after a week of attacks, as fighting also rages in and around Ras Lanuf.

Libyan rebels moved to consolidate control over the country after storming Moammar Gadhafi's fortified Bab al-Aziziya compound in Tripoli, as the National Transition Council said it would organize $2.4 billion in international aid for Libya.
A suicide bombing in Damascus kills Syrian Defence Minister Dawoud Rajha and other senior security officials.
Syrian Prime Minister Riad Hijab defects from President Bashar Assad's regime, a humiliating blow that suggests fissures reaching deeper into the ruling system.
Thousands of Yemenis protest in Sanaa demanding President Ali Abdullah Saleh step down after 32 years in power, in the first large-scale public challenge to his rule.
Yemeni government forces opened fire with anti-aircraft guns and automatic weapons on tens of thousands of anti-government protesters in Sanaa, killing at least 26 and wounding more than 200.
